sentence_stem: Yesterday my brother asked me for help,
correct_completion: so I helped him with his homework.
full_sentence: Yesterday my brother asked me for help, so I helped him with his homework.
acceptable_variants: so I decided to help him.
and I helped him finish it.

options.text: so I cooked dinner for everyone.
options.why_wrong: Cooking dinner does not respond to his request. After 'so', the clause should show what the speaker did because of the request.

options.text: so I helped him with his homework.
and he wants to play football today.
options.why_wrong: This adds a new wish from the brother but does not answer the request for help.
This describes another past event but does not connect to the request for help.

grammar_focus: Past simple regular verbs (-ed) in cause-and-effect sentences
explanation: After 'so', we need a clause that shows the result of the first part. Regular past verbs add -ed, as in 'asked' and 'helped'. Portuguese speakers sometimes forget to add -ed to regular verbs, because Portuguese verb endings change in a different way.
translation: Ontem meu irmão me pediu ajuda, então eu o ajudei com a lição de casa.
